The DOE/ NNSA FY22 SSMP identifies DARHT as a weapons mission–critical facility and states that there is a need to modernize DARHT to support weapons modernization efforts and support Counterterrorism and Counterproliferation (CTCP) experimental validation efforts [NNSA, 2022]. The 2018 NPR, however, states that the nuclear weapons infrastruc- ture has suffered the effects of age and underfunding with no margin for further delay in recapitalizing the physical infrastructure [DOD, 2018]. To address these national policy concerns, responsive action is required at DARHT. The facility is an indispensable, strategic component of the nation’s nuclear weapons infrastructure that must be recapitalized and modernized. It is critically important that the systems supporting this experimental capability are reliable and resilient. The NNSA has identified DARHT Sustainment and Modernization projects to address aging of the DARHT Complex along with other issues currently limiting or threatening the capability and capacity of DARHT [NNSA, 2022]. Further, the NNSA states that a strategy addressing the goals of these DARHT Complex projects to extend DARHT reliability and resilience, in- crease the quality and quantity of DARHT data, and enable hydrodynamic measurements in complex environments is required [NNSA, 2023]. This DCX Strategy, with its three overarching priorities, has been created to address specific NNSA requirements for DARHT Sustainment and Modernization. Axis 2 linear injector 7 Photo credit: David J. Woodfin Varying configurations were studied during the conceptual design phase of DARHT. Initially considered were two machines with an adjustable geometry capability, and with low-energy/large-spot–size, pulsed-power diodes of the type then in use at the United Kingdom’s Atomic Weapons Establishment (AWE). The same two machines, now fixed in place, were considered in the second concept. This configuration evolved to include an underground control and diagnostic bunker. Later, in order to increase the x-ray dose and decrease the x-ray spot size, two linear induction accelerators (LIAs) based on the Flash X-Ray (FXR) machine at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) were considered. 8 DCX STRATEGY DCX Introduction Radiography was a nascent but key capability in the development of the first implosion weapon, and it has evolved continuously since the Manhattan Project. The Pulsed High-Energy Radiographic Machine Emitting X Rays (PHER- MEX) was the first major step forward in U.S. radiographic capabilities. Exploratory work began soon after Trinity, with operations spanning from 1963–2004. Through continuous R&D, upgrades during 41 years of radiography have included several beam energy improvements, inclusion of graded collimators, the move to digital cameras, and a rudimentary dual-pulse capability.
